# Zedu Demo Day Live Buzz Presentation Run Sheet & Recruiter Onboarding Workflow (Revision 3)

*A Practical Operational Blueprint for Bootcamp Career Services, Academic Leads, and Event Hosts*  
**Platform:** Zedu Buzz & Channels ([https://zedu.chat](https://zedu.chat))  
**Date Checked:** 22 October 2026  
**Source & Methodology:** Grounded strictly in static code analysis of `Cybertron-HNG/zedu-fe` (`cybertron-integration` @ 214cb29). Steps derived from code inspection are flagged for staging verification prior to live event execution.

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Core Requirements

A virtual Demo Day connects graduating technical talent directly with hiring partners, engineering managers, and prospective employers. 

This run sheet outlines the operational framework for running a 2-hour virtual Demo Day on **Zedu Buzz**, complete with verified channel routing, guest recruiter invitation templates, discussion thread Q&A management, and student privacy consent protocols.

---

## 2. 2-Hour Virtual Demo Day Operational Run Sheet

| Time | Duration | Segment | Platform Location | Operational Actions |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **T - 15m** | 15 min | Speaker Green Room | Private Prep Channel | Presenter audio check. Verify camera, microphone, and screen-sharing permissions. |
| **T + 00m** | 10 min | Welcome & Address | `#demo-day-main` (`/[org]/home/channels/[id]`) | Lead instructor clicks **Start a buzz** (`call-button.tsx` line 33). Welcomes recruiters and reviews agenda. |
| **T + 10m** | 45 min | Presentations: Batch A (5 Squads)| Native Buzz Session | 7-min pitch + 2-min Q&A per squad. Students broadcast slides via **Start screen share** (`buzzSidePanel.tsx` line 229). |
| **T + 55m** | 10 min | Portfolio Intermission | `#job-opportunities` & Files | Employers review candidate portfolios in Files via per-file sharing links (`CreateShareModal.tsx`). |
| **T + 65m** | 45 min | Presentations: Batch B (5 Squads)| Native Buzz Session | 7-min pitch + 2-min Q&A per squad. Questions captured in message discussion threads. |
| **T + 110m**| 10 min | Closing Remarks & Next Steps | Native Buzz Session | Coordinator summarizes talent hiring availability; call concluded via call menu. |

---

## 3. Verified Zedu Buzz Presentation Protocols

Native Zedu Buzz provides integrated audio/video collaboration powered by the Agora WebRTC SDK:

### A. Launching & Joining Live Sessions
1. In the designated presentation channel, click **Start a buzz** located in the channel header (`buzz-management/call-button.tsx` line 33).
2. For attendees entering the channel while a session is active, the call button tooltip reads **Join ongoing buzz** (`call-button.tsx` line 33); clicking the call button connects the user to the session.
3. Coordinators can copy the direct call anchor by opening the buzz menu and selecting **Copy buzz link** (`buzz-menu.tsx` line 44). Note: this provides the Buzz room anchor; the channel itself is accessed via its standard route.

### B. Screen Sharing & Moderation Controls
- Presenters broadcast live demos and slides using the **Start screen share** / **Stop screen share** toggle button (`buzzSidePanel.tsx` line 229, `chatBuzzSidePanel.tsx` line 266).
- Event hosts can mute non-speaking participants using **Mute participants** in the meeting menu (`meeting/buzz-menu.tsx` line 237).

### C. Threaded Discussion Q&A
- During live pitches, recruiters type inquiries under the pinned squad announcement post.
- Attendees and judges open the thread discussion drawer via the thread action handlers in `ChannelMessage/more.tsx` (lines 57 and 62), keeping questions and feedback organized without cluttering the main channel.

### D. Automated Session Summary
- *Documentation Note:* Zedu features automated post-session meeting summaries per official product documentation (`zedu.chat/products/buzz`); live transcript and summary generation should be verified in your specific staging deployment.

---

## 4. Recruiter Onboarding & Email Invitation Workflow

### Verified Access Model (No Separate Guest Role):
In `zedu-fe`, workspaces do not feature an unauthenticated public guest role. Recruiters and hiring managers are added to the workspace as **Members** via the standard **Invite People** flow in user management (`[org]/home/settings/users`). 

*Security Best Practice:* Following Demo Day, career leads should remove recruiter member accounts to maintain internal workspace privacy.

### Accurate Channel Link Sharing:
Because message menus provide a message link (`ChannelMessage/more.tsx` line 181) rather than a channel link, event coordinators should:
1. Copy the full channel URL directly from the browser address bar: `https://zedu.chat/[org]/home/channels/[id]`
2. OR Pin a "Demo Day Welcome & Agenda" message in the channel, click its 3-dot menu, select **Copy link**, and share the pinned message link.

### Template 1: Recruiter Invitation (Sent 7 Days Before Demo Day)
```text
Subject: Exclusive Invitation: [Academy Name] Virtual Demo Day & Tech Talent Showcase

Dear [Recruiter / Partner Name],

On [Date] at 2:00 PM WAT, our graduating cohort of software engineers and product designers will showcase their live capstone projects at the [Academy Name] Virtual Demo Day.

Demo Day is hosted directly on Zedu, giving you a live view of candidate presentations, project source code, and portfolio assets in one unified workspace.

Event Details:
- Date & Time: [Date] | 2:00 PM – 4:00 PM WAT
- Event Channel: [Coordinator: Paste full browser URL https://zedu.chat/[org]/home/channels/[id]]
- Candidate Portfolio Index: [Insert file share link to Master Candidate Directory from Files]

To confirm your attendance and receive your workspace member invite link, please RSVP by replying to this email.

Warm regards,
[Your Name]  
Career Placement Director, [Academy Name]
```

### Template 2: Day-of-Event Entry Guide (Sent 2 Hours Before Kickoff)
```text
Subject: Starting at 2 PM: [Academy Name] Demo Day Live Stage Link

Hi [Hiring Partner Name],

Our graduating engineering squads take the stage in 2 hours!

Fast-Track Entry Steps:
1. Log in to your invited account and open our event channel: [Insert exact channel URL]
2. In the top-right header, click the call button (shows tooltip "Join ongoing buzz") to enter the live stage.
3. Use the discussion thread under each squad's announcement for questions during presentations.

See you on the main stage at 2:00 PM prompt!
```

---

## 5. Student Privacy Consent & Pre-Flight Verification Checklist

- [ ] **Methodology Notice:** All steps derived from `zedu-fe` code inspection; test the complete flow on a test account prior to event day.
- [ ] **Student Privacy Opt-In:** Verified written student consent before sharing any project repositories, resumes, or portfolios with external partners.
- [ ] **Dedicated Presentation Channel:** Created at `/[org]/home/channels/[id]`. Channel URL copied directly from browser address bar.
- [ ] **Recruiter Invites:** Dispatched via **Invite People** as Members; calendar reminder set to remove recruiter access post-event.
- [ ] **Technical Run-Through:** Screen sharing tested using **Start screen share** (`buzzSidePanel.tsx` line 229) in private green room.
- [ ] **Threaded Q&A Rules:** Welcome announcement pinned with instructions to use thread drawer for questions (`ChannelMessage/more.tsx` lines 57, 62).

---

changesToCheck.body:
I checked round 2 against my round-1 points and Adele's, on zedu-fe cybertron-integration 214cb29.

Fixed:
- The channel route is now /[org]/home/channels/[id]. Correct.
- Recruiters are onboarded with 'Invite People' in user management before the event, and 'free instant browser entry' is gone.
- 'Join ongoing buzz' is now correctly the call button's tooltip (call-button.tsx line 33), and 'Copy buzz link' is correct at line 44.
- 'End buzz' and the 440px detail are removed, the summary is now 'per product documentation, confirm in your deployment', and a student opt-in consent step was added.

Still wrong:
1. The 'Copy link' the invitations rely on isn't a channel link. ChannelMessage/more.tsx line 181 is 'Copy link' in a message's menu, so it copies a link to one message, not to the channel. Either tell organisers to share the channel URL from the address bar (/[org]/home/channels/[id]), or link a pinned message and say so.
2. The thread action is cited as more.tsx line 181, but line 181 is that 'Copy link' item, not a thread action. Cite the real thread entry point, or describe it without a line number.
3. Screen share: the control's label is 'Start screen share' / 'Stop screen share' (buzzSidePanel.tsx line 229, chatBuzzSidePanel.tsx line 266), not 'Screen Share'. Use the real label.
4. Unverified features are still presented as available: 'a dedicated attendee invite link', 'guest workspace access invite' (I find no Guest role in src) and a 'view-only portfolio index link from File Management' (no view-only or invite-link code in src/app/(client)/[org]). Remove them or mark them 'to confirm'.
5. Adele asked for a tested recruiter path. Nothing here shows an actual test, so the run sheet should say that the steps come from the code, not from a live test.

Score 6: the structure and most labels are now right, but the copy-ready invitations still depend on a link the app doesn't give for channels, and some access features aren't shown to exist.

Revision 2 fixes the route format, adds consent, and removes some unsupported claims, but several review points remain. 'Copy link' in the invitation is still attributed to the channel; the cited Buzz link action copies a Buzz link, not necessarily the channel URL. The text still treats 'Join ongoing buzz' as words to click, labels the control 'Screen Share' instead of the app's 'Start screen share', and mentions an unverified attendee invite link and view-only portfolio index. Please correct those details, mark code-derived steps as untested, and verify the actual recruiter sign-in/channel-access path before calling the invitations ready.

tasks.title: Audit the six core journeys against WCAG 2.2 and deliver a reproducible issue log
tasks.description:
Set at 60 (top of research range) because it covers six journeys, manual assistive-technology testing rather than an automated scan, and a retest plan. Judge the scope in review.

Work in a test workspace with synthetic records only. No real learner, teacher or personal data, and no screenshot showing a real name, email or message.

Six journeys, each start to finish, on desktop and on a narrow mobile viewport:
1. Organiser creates a workspace and first channel.
2. Organiser invites a member and sets a role.
3. Learner accepts an invite and lands in the workspace for the first time.
4. Learner joins a live Buzz session and leaves it.
5. Learner opens a file or assignment, submits or replies, then finds it again later.
6. End of cohort: organiser exports or hands over, and a member is removed.

Test with at least two of: keyboard only, NVDA or VoiceOver, 200% zoom, mobile screen reader. Record which was used for each finding.

Pay particular attention to the WCAG 2.2 criteria audits usually skip: 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured, 2.5.7 Dragging Movements, 2.5.8 Target Size, 3.3.7 Redundant Entry, 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication.

Deliverable: one issue log in the attachment. Per issue: journey and step, what the person was trying to do, what happened, exact reproduction steps, browser and assistive technology with version, WCAG 2.2 criterion and level, impact in plain words, priority (blocker/high/medium/low), and whether it came from automation or manual testing. Separate those two clearly. Add a short section of checks that passed, so it is not only failures, and a retest plan naming the step to repeat per finding.

Do not publish, badge or claim conformance anywhere public in this task. Findings stay internal until the team verifies them.

No real attendee addresses, automatic invitations or calendar account writes. Explain that re-importing a revised file may duplicate an event and provide a manual replace/check procedure; do not promise automatic update/cancellation behavior. Done when the generator, editable inputs, three valid .ics fixtures, reproducible checks and matching text/checklist are attached. Fictional examples must not be usable as real meeting invitations. tasks.title: Write the spreadsheet-to-Zedu migration kit: which column goes where, and what never moves
tasks.description:

Write the kit that answers that for one program manager, in plain language.

1. A mapping table. One row per column a real tracker carries: learner name, phone, cohort, week, session date, attendance, assignment, score, fee status, notes. For each one, where it goes in Zedu, or 'stays in your spreadsheet' plus the reason. Use only what the live site and pricing page show: channels, threads, announcements, files, assignment discussions, live classes and recordings, AI study assistant, analytics. Where you cannot confirm something, write [CONFIRM] and the exact question to ask.

2. A 45-minute migration session, split 15/15/15, with who does what. Assume no technical help.

3. Two messages to learners, one before the move and one after. WhatsApp length, warm, no hype.

4. What not to migrate. Name the columns that have no home in Zedu, so nobody promises a feature that does not exist.

5. A one-page check the manager runs a week later: three yes/no questions that show whether the cohort actually moved.

Rules: no invented features, no retention or export promises, no claim that Zedu replaces the spreadsheet in every case. Every Zedu feature you name carries a URL and the date you checked it.

Done when every column is accounted for, the 'what not to migrate' list is explicit, and the week-later check is three questions, not a survey.
tasks.rationale: Many bootcamps run the cohort on a spreadsheet plus a WhatsApp group, and the switch stalls because nobody can say which column goes where. A plain mapping kit lowers that switching cost for the exact audience the brief asks us to acquire, and nothing on the board covers it.

currentDelivery.body:
Checked every entry on the academy's own live page on 24 Oct 2026: 20 rows (19 academies; Loctech has campuses in both Port Harcourt and Enugu) across Lagos (8), Abuja (4), Port Harcourt (6) and Enugu (2). Each row has the published address, website, curriculum focus, cohort length or intake info as stated, and an official contact. The verification log lists the exact URL for every row.

Two honest limits: (1) I could verify 20, not 30. The task says 'strictly zero unverified entries', so I didn't pad the list; the 13 candidates I rejected are listed with their reasons. (2) No verified page publicly names a training director or admissions lead, so the decision-maker column says 'not public' plus the official admissions email or phone. I didn't take names from personal profiles. Batch sizes are given only where a page states them (most don't). Nobody was contacted.
